First up, I really liked this game. The concept was fun, the execution was good, the multiplayer aspect brilliant.
Why don't I recommend the game?
1) Grind. Far too much of it.
This game is for casual players. Let them jump in. Pat their backs a bit, let them down gently when they fail. Make it fun and amusing. Keep them engaged.
The grind in this game is just too much to enjoy it.
I played 2p with my partner. Unlocks were so slow, after a couple of hours I had to beg my partner to play another couple of games, yet we didn't unlock any new recipes. We didn't unlock any new locations. It was all just rinse and repeat. And we'd get to day 8-9 and become overwhelmed because there's just 2 of us. 
2) Difficulty scaling. I'd love to give this a shot just me, not with another person, lets run a successful restaurant. Give me a bot or two to help me out. Give me something to let me stress out a bit with and focus on efficiency.

I don't feel like I've even scraped what this game has to offer, but I simply am unable to continue because the only person I have to play it with me got bored after a few rounds of rinse and repeat.

Honestly, unless you're playing with other hardcore gamers, I wouldn't even bother trying.

Keep in mind, this was my own experience with the game, and the experience I felt feels very specific and I've tried nearly everything to fix it despite the new "Fix"

Okay, I hate to give another negative review. However, I feel it makes more sense to weight it that way. To be CLEAR, I do still have fun with this game. I do still tepidly recommend it, but I think most of the reviewers didn't give enough details on the pros and cons of the game.

In terms of pros, the game is fun. You and your friends can easily get into a rhythm of chaotically managing the restaruant and feeding customers. It also isn't a hard game to learn the mechanics for (more on that in a min.) And you will find yourself having enough rounds to really rack up some game time.

So why am I giving it a negative review? First, I don't know why but the instructions aren't clear on how to complete certain tasks or make food. My brother and I both played together and gave up on Pizza after about 5 minutes of practice. I think a visual showing that "Hey you kneed once for Pizza and kneeding twice is overdone" like in Overcooked would help. Second, the game suffers from crowded kitchen/dinning spaces. While I get it, it's supposed to be realistic. The game is a struggle because you run out of room so easily because there's no balancing for the dinning area/kitchen. When making dumplings, my brother prefers a small work space due to how limited the counter space is. However, when we're trying to destress the dining area due to the customer rushes, it gets difficult. The biggest issue though is the No Win RNG on every 3 days. Every 3 successful shifts forces you to pick Option A

EDIT: There was a big update soon after this review, so take that into account. I haven't played it, but apparently it adds some aspect of permanent progression among other things.

Short version: I have never liked these "control chaos" type of games that much. It seems to be a good one of those. It's fun with friends, just not for me.

Going into more detail, this is not a management sim. The game is not about building the restaurant of your dreams and improving it with the profits. It's about trying to keep up with the constantly increasing demand until you eventually fail. I like to have at least some meta-progression in my games, here you can at best start with some extra benefits but you'll still fail eventually. Maybe workshop mods could change this, I didn't check since we just played with normal settings.

That said, with friends the serving part is fun. Even though the cooking is always just a variation on pressing use button until the food is ready. There's plenty of cooperation needed to make it through the later days. You can even automate some of your kitchen if you're lucky enough to get the required upgrades.

I can recommend this if you like these types of games, especially if you have friends to play with. Like I said, I personally don't really enjoy doing the same thing from the start over and over again for a long time.

Between this, and overcooked, overcooked wins hands down. This game is made to be as tedious as possible. Upgrades are similar in names, but different in functionality (robot buffer vs moper is the most egregious example where one buffs movement speed, and the other cleans floors), while other "upgrades" are hands down downgrades (bar stool, buffet). Single player experience is miserable, and if a game is only fun when played with friends then it's a ♥♥♥♥ game, because anything done with friends is fun.

As far as I can tell, the way to build super busy automated restaurants like you see in screenshots is to make mass copies of items using unintuitive research bench + file cabinet mechanics.

If you don't want to fiddle with silly metagaming hijinks you have to barely scrape by while focusing on keeping menus as simple and limited as possible.

I don't really see how either of those options are any fun.

I can't recommend this game unless y ou get it for less than five dollars. To be honest, it feels like it's in early access. Unless it's unlocked much later, there's no way to expand the space of your restaurant, and you are forced to choose one of the randomly generated layouts. Some foods don't make sense (like the pumpkin pie is personal, so you'd have to make three for a three topper table). If you are doing something greasy like steaks, you have to pray that you get the mop or your floors are going to be gross. Solo or multiplayer, it's just punishing.

All of this could be mitigated if it had the ability to adjust difficulty base game, but it's not. There is a mod available, but I'm so frustrated with the base game I'm not going to bother. I just wanted to play a chill restaurant game with my friends. The final nail in the coffin is that this game is $20 full price. Come on, now.
